reason: I’ll start with dissolved volatiles and falling pressure to work toward the steam-rich atmosphere.
expectation: Lower pressure may release gases, including water vapor, from the melt.

alternatives.reason: Convection may help form the rocky coast, but I’ll follow the water first.

effect: Falling pressure released dissolved volatiles as bubbles; convection is the only offered combination to continue.
reaction: The clarification that outgassing moves existing elements is useful.
reason: I’ll follow the only available combination to bring heat and melt toward the surface.
expectation: Convection may move hot molten rock upward, helping form the lava and solid-rock coast.

effect: Upwelling brings hot rock toward the surface, opening paths for gas release and cooling.
reaction: The connection between interior movement and surface heat loss is clear.
reason: I’ll combine the bubbles with upwelling rock to continue toward an atmosphere.
expectation: The rising rock may carry the separated gases toward the surface, releasing them into the atmosphere.

alternatives.reason: Cooling the upwelling rock could advance the coast goal, but I’ll follow the gas first.

effect: The bubbles escaped through the surface as volcanic gas, providing material for an atmosphere.
reaction: The reminder that the gas is not breathable makes the early atmosphere more concrete.
reason: I’ll use gravity to retain the volcanic gases and pursue the atmosphere goal.
expectation: Gravity may hold the released gases around Earth, forming an early atmosphere.

alternatives.reason: Cooling the upwelling rock could advance the coast goal, but I’ll finish following the gas first.

effect: The released gases formed a steam-rich atmosphere, completing that goal; the coast remains.
reaction: It is useful to see that Earth retains only part of the released gas.
reason: The only offered combination should help cool the upwelling rock toward a solid coast.
expectation: The hot rock may lose heat to space and begin to solidify.

effect: The exposed lava has begun solidifying while hot rock remains mobile beneath it.
reaction: The contrast between the solid skin and mobile rock below is clear.
reason: I’ll follow the only offered combination to continue cooling the surface toward a rocky coast.
expectation: Further cooling may solidify more of the lava skin into rock.

effect: Cooling formed a basaltic crust, but the lava-and-rock coast goal remains.
reaction: The local nature of this solidification is a useful distinction.
reason: I’ll follow the only offered combination to connect the crust with continuing molten-rock movement.
expectation: Convection may bring fresh lava alongside or through the crust, helping form the coast.

effect: Convection fractured the crust, creating possible pathways for later water.
reaction: The link between volcanic activity and future water pathways is intriguing.
reason: I’ll follow the only offered combination to bring upwelling rock together with the fractured crust.
expectation: Fresh molten rock may reach the fractured surface, creating a mixture of lava and solid crust.

effect: Fresh lava moving through fractured crust completed the coast goal, leaving adjacent hot and cooler surfaces.
reaction: The contrast gives the future arrival of rain a concrete setting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following dissolved volatiles from bubbles to a steam-rich atmosphere made outgassing understandable without implying that it creates water’s hydrogen.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive cooling steps felt somewhat repetitive, even though they distinguished a solidifying skin from basaltic crust.

surprise.text: Fractures made by continued heat and motion can provide routes for later water.

arbitrary.text: Combining the young crust with convection initially felt somewhat abstract, but the resulting fractures gave it a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how rain interacts with the contrasting lava and solid crust, and how water moves through the fractures.
